sections.heading: La regla general: Make vs. Do
sections.body: Tanto 'make' como 'do' se traducen como 'hacer' en español, pero en inglés siguen colocaciones fijas: **'Make'** suele referirse a crear, producir, construir o generar algo nuevo (un resultado o decisión). **'Do'** suele asociarse con actividades, tareas, rutinas, obligaciones y procesos de trabajo.

sections.heading: Colocaciones frecuentes con Make
sections.body: *Make a decision, make a mistake, make money, make a suggestion, make progress, make an effort, make a phone call, make a reservation, make friends, make an excuse, make sense*.

sections.heading: Colocaciones frecuentes con Do
sections.body: *Do homework, do research, do your best, do exercise, do the dishes, do someone a favor, do business, do damage, do a course, do well/badly*.

examples.english: He does scientific research at the university.
examples.note: Investigación / trabajo de estudio → se usa 'do'.

examples.english: We made a few minor mistakes.
I will do my best to help you.

quiz.question: Which of the following sentences uses 'make' or 'do' correctly?
options: I did a big mistake on the exam.
I made a big mistake on the exam.
I made the dishes after dinner.
Can you make me a favor?
quiz.explanation: 'Make a mistake' is a fixed collocation. In English you 'do the dishes' and 'do someone a favor'.
